bibl.title: Cell-Type Specific Features of Circular RNA Expression

person.p: the tag layer; a sentence written by the tagger about the paper, always anchored to a quotation but not itself a quotation

span.label: CIRCULAR RNA - a class of molecules that was transcriptional noise until an alignment threshold was replaced by an average, and is now claimed to be the predominant isoform at hundreds of loci
span.quote: Circular RNA transcripts had been reported previously for a handful of genes. With the possible exceptions of the circular RNA isoforms of the Sry gene in mouse testis [2] and the muscleblind gene in Drosophila melanogaster [3] these were generally thought to be rare RNA species, perhaps the result of transcriptional noise.

span.label: how much circular RNA there is, whether its expression is regulated, and whether the class survives the test that it is a splicing error
span.quote: Using an improved computational approach for circular RNA identification, we found widespread circular RNA expression in Drosophila melanogaster and estimate that in humans, circular RNA may account for 1% as many molecules as poly(A) RNA.

span.label: an alignment method that averages quality scores instead of thresholding them, a much larger catalogue of circles, and the finding that the circular:linear ratio is cell-type specific
span.quote: To improve our sensitivity and specificity in detecting circular isoforms, we developed improved bioinformatic and statistical methods that enabled more reliable discrimination between bona fide evidence of exon scrambling and artifacts introduced by high throughput sequencing and sequence homology within a gene. This improved performance allowed us to detect a more extensive catalog of circular RNA than previously reported, including small RNA circles, RNA circles formed by non-canonical splicing of short exons and noncoding RNAs.

span.label: existence
span.quote: Using an improved computational approach for circular RNA identification, we found widespread circular RNA expression in Drosophila melanogaster and estimate that in humans, circular RNA may account for 1% as many molecules as poly(A) RNA.

span.label: circularisation as a regulated part of the gene expression programme - the repertoire, the ratio and even the splice isoforms varying by cell type
span.quote: Analysis of data from the ENCODE consortium revealed that the repertoire of genes expressing circular RNA, the ratio of circular to linear transcripts for each gene, and even the pattern of splice isoforms of circular RNAs from each gene were cell-type specific.

span.label: a new bioinformatic and statistical approach applied to ENCODE RNA-Seq data and Drosophila brain RNA, with qPCR quantification, and an explicit test of the noise hypothesis
span.term: a new bioinformatic and statistical approach applied to ENCODE RNA-Seq data and Drosophila brain RNA, with qPCR quantification, and an explicit test of the noise hypothesis
span.quote: A major challenge in bioinformatic and statistical identification of novel RNA isoforms, particularly circular RNA, involves distinguishing bona fide evidence of scrambled exons in RNA from confounding factors such as sequence degeneracy at exon boundaries and sequencing errors. To address these challenges and to identify circular isoforms from public ENCODE RNA-Seq data, we developed a new bioinformatic approach.

span.label: THE METHODOLOGICAL CHANGE IS EXACTLY A THRESHOLD: the method `REFRAINS FROM QUALITATIVE HARD THRESHOLDING of read alignment quality, and instead COMPUTES STATISTICAL AVERAGES of alignment quality scores`. The molecules did not change. THE CUT DID
span.quote: The main idea behind our computational method is that it refrains from qualitative hard thresholding of read alignment quality, and instead computes statistical averages of alignment quality scores.

span.label: and the reason the class was invisible is stated with a number attached: `although de novo splicing detection algorithms have been used in MORE THAN A THOUSAND PUBLISHED STUDIES ... most instances of scrambled exons in human RNAs, and thus the circular species that they represent, HAD ELUDED DETECTION`
span.quote: Indeed, although de novo splicing detection algorithms have been used in more than a thousand published studies, including studies aimed at identifying gene fusions and internal tandem duplications, most instances of scrambled exons in human RNAs, and thus the circular species that they represent, had eluded detection.

span.label: THE CATALOGUE IS A PROPERTY OF THE DETECTOR AND THE PAPER SAYS SO IN ITS OWN CONTRIBUTION SENTENCE: `to IMPROVE OUR SENSITIVITY AND SPECIFICITY in detecting circular isoforms, we developed improved bioinformatic and statistical methods. THIS IMPROVED PERFORMANCE ALLOWED US TO DETECT A MORE EXTENSIVE CATALOG than previously reported`. Every count in the paper is a count at one operating point
span.quote: To improve our sensitivity and specificity in detecting circular isoforms, we developed improved bioinformatic and statistical methods that enabled more reliable discrimination between bona fide evidence of exon scrambling and artifacts introduced by high throughput sequencing and sequence homology within a gene. This improved performance allowed us to detect a more extensive catalog of circular RNA than previously reported, including small RNA circles, RNA circles formed by non-canonical splicing of short exons and noncoding RNAs.

span.label: the headline abundance is hedged twice over: circular RNA `MAY ACCOUNT FOR 1% AS MANY MOLECULES AS POLY(A) RNA` - a ratio to another measured quantity, in the cells they investigated, from qPCR plus RNA-Seq
span.quote: Using an improved computational approach for circular RNA identification, we found widespread circular RNA expression in Drosophila melanogaster and estimate that in humans, circular RNA may account for 1% as many molecules as poly(A) RNA.

span.label: and the independent confirmations use A DIFFERENT SAMPLE AND A DIFFERENT PREPARATION: `1025 of 1319` of the previously described circles were recovered by RNase R-treated sequencing - and the paper flags the difference itself, `the more recent report focused on FIBROBLASTS, while we previously analyzed RNA isolated from LEUKOCYTES AND PEDIATRIC LEUKEMIAS`
span.quote: In the former report, a large majority of the circular isoforms we had described (1025 of 1319) were also identified by deep sequencing of RNase R-treated RNA. This overlap in circles identified in these two studies is noteworthy because the more recent report focused on fibroblasts, while we previously analyzed RNA isolated from leukocytes and pediatric leukemias.

span.label: THE NOISE HYPOTHESIS, STATED AS A PREDICTION AND THEN TESTED: if circles were dysfunctional splicing, circle detection should rise with linear expression from the same gene
span.note: eliminates: the artefact reading of the entire class - `WE FOUND NO EVIDENCE OF SUCH A RELATIONSHIP`. The prediction is stated BEFORE the result, and it is the test that would have destroyed the paper's object · outcome: held
span.quote: We tested the hypothesis that circular RNAs might be the result of a background “noise” level of dysfunctional splicing. Under this model, we would expect a positive relationship between linear RNA isoform expression from a given gene and the probability of detecting a circular RNA isoform from that gene. We found no evidence of such a relationship

span.label: independent confirmation by a different preparation - RNase R digestion, which destroys linear RNA - and in a different cell type
span.note: eliminates: the objection that the circles are an artefact of one pipeline: `1025 of 1319` were recovered, and the paper notes the samples differ (fibroblasts against leukocytes and pediatric leukemias), which makes the overlap harder rather than easier · outcome: held
span.quote: In the former report, a large majority of the circular isoforms we had described (1025 of 1319) were also identified by deep sequencing of RNase R-treated RNA. This overlap in circles identified in these two studies is noteworthy because the more recent report focused on fibroblasts, while we previously analyzed RNA isolated from leukocytes and pediatric leukemias.

span.label: agreement with a thirty-year-old estimate obtained by a completely unrelated instrument
span.note: eliminates: sequencing-specific artefact as the explanation of the abundance - electron microscopy shares no failure mode with RNA-Seq · outcome: held
span.quote: qPCR quantification and extensive analysis of RNA-Seq data has allowed us to estimate that the number of circular RNA molecules is roughly 1% of the number of poly(A) molecules in the cells we investigated. This estimate is remarkably similar to a report published more than 30 years ago, which found physical evidence of circular RNA by examining cellular RNA by electron microscopy

span.label: circular RNA
span.quote: Circular RNA transcripts had been reported previously for a handful of genes. With the possible exceptions of the circular RNA isoforms of the Sry gene in mouse testis [2] and the muscleblind gene in Drosophila melanogaster [3] these were generally thought to be rare RNA species, perhaps the result of transcriptional noise.

span.label: transcriptional noise
span.quote: Circular RNA transcripts had been reported previously for a handful of genes. With the possible exceptions of the circular RNA isoforms of the Sry gene in mouse testis [2] and the muscleblind gene in Drosophila melanogaster [3] these were generally thought to be rare RNA species, perhaps the result of transcriptional noise.

span.label: hard thresholding
span.quote: The main idea behind our computational method is that it refrains from qualitative hard thresholding of read alignment quality, and instead computes statistical averages of alignment quality scores.

span.label: scrambled exons
span.quote: Indeed, although de novo splicing detection algorithms have been used in more than a thousand published studies, including studies aimed at identifying gene fusions and internal tandem duplications, most instances of scrambled exons in human RNAs, and thus the circular species that they represent, had eluded detection.

span.label: RNase R
span.quote: The ubiquitous expression of circular RNA in human and mouse cells has now been independently confirmed by high throughput sequencing of the RNase R treated, ribosomal-depleted fraction of RNA, combined with a previously published informatic algorithm to identify circular RNA [7] as well as by a second report characterizing RNA after ribosomal RNA depletion

span.label: electron microscopy
span.quote: qPCR quantification and extensive analysis of RNA-Seq data has allowed us to estimate that the number of circular RNA molecules is roughly 1% of the number of poly(A) molecules in the cells we investigated. This estimate is remarkably similar to a report published more than 30 years ago, which found physical evidence of circular RNA by examining cellular RNA by electron microscopy

span.label: circular RNA, BEFORE: `generally thought to be RARE RNA SPECIES, PERHAPS THE RESULT OF TRANSCRIPTIONAL NOISE`. A class of molecules whose status was NOISE - not unmeasured, but categorised as error
span.quote: Circular RNA transcripts had been reported previously for a handful of genes. With the possible exceptions of the circular RNA isoforms of the Sry gene in mouse testis [2] and the muscleblind gene in Drosophila melanogaster [3] these were generally thought to be rare RNA species, perhaps the result of transcriptional noise.

span.label: circular RNA, AFTER: `previously thought to be very rare, ARE ACTUALLY A PERVASIVE FEATURE of eukaryotic gene expression programs; indeed, THE MAJOR RNA ISOFORM FROM HUNDREDS OF HUMAN GENES IS A CIRCLE`. Same molecules, same data type, one changed alignment rule
span.quote: Last year, we reported that circular RNA isoforms, previously thought to be very rare, are actually a pervasive feature of eukaryotic gene expression programs; indeed, the major RNA isoform from hundreds of human genes is a circle.

span.label: `detected`, AS OPERATIONALISED HERE - what survives a method that AVERAGES alignment quality instead of THRESHOLDING it. `A thousand published studies` used the thresholded algorithms and the class `HAD ELUDED DETECTION`
span.quote: The main idea behind our computational method is that it refrains from qualitative hard thresholding of read alignment quality, and instead computes statistical averages of alignment quality scores.

span.label: the noise hypothesis, STATED AS A PREDICTION AND THEN TESTED: `under this model, WE WOULD EXPECT A POSITIVE RELATIONSHIP between linear RNA isoform expression from a given gene and the probability of detecting a circular RNA isoform from that gene. WE FOUND NO EVIDENCE OF SUCH A RELATIONSHIP`
span.quote: We tested the hypothesis that circular RNAs might be the result of a background “noise” level of dysfunctional splicing. Under this model, we would expect a positive relationship between linear RNA isoform expression from a given gene and the probability of detecting a circular RNA isoform from that gene. We found no evidence of such a relationship

span.label: extends → salzman2012, this group's own discovery paper - `LAST YEAR, WE REPORTED that circular RNA isoforms ... are actually a pervasive feature`. The corpus holds it at 62 tags
span.quote: Last year, we reported that circular RNA isoforms, previously thought to be very rare, are actually a pervasive feature of eukaryotic gene expression programs; indeed, the major RNA isoform from hundreds of human genes is a circle.

span.label: contradicts → the prior classification of circular RNA as transcriptional noise - tested directly, with the prediction stated first
span.quote: We tested the hypothesis that circular RNAs might be the result of a background “noise” level of dysfunctional splicing. Under this model, we would expect a positive relationship between linear RNA isoform expression from a given gene and the probability of detecting a circular RNA isoform from that gene. We found no evidence of such a relationship
